claim: On ISS FLEX, large n-heptane droplets burning in ordinary air lost their visible flame through radiative extinction but kept burning in a second, low-temperature 'cool flame' stage with no visible emission, until extinction at a smaller size; small droplets burned in a single classical stage. conditions: n-heptane droplets (base case 3.91 mm); 21% O2, 79% N2; 1 atm; still air; ISS (FLEX)

location: Tests FLEX-069 to FLEX-087 and FLEX-209 to FLEX-221

conditions: Methanol droplets 2.5 to 2.6 mm; 15% O2; balance N2 with 0, 32% CO2 or 30% He; about 1 atm; quiescent; ISS FLEX
source: NASA PSI table PSI-69 (FLEX experimental table)
location: Tests FLEX-066, FLEX-068, FLEX-163, FLEX-164, FLEX-245
confidence_note: Only one to two tests per gas mix at matched size; larger droplets show the same order. Helium cools the flame by conduction and CO2 by radiation and heat capacity; FLEX was designed to test such suppressants. 'Volume burned' computed by BurnBook

conditions: n-dodecane droplets about 4 mm; 21% O2 in N2 (some tests 17% O2 or 29 to 59% He); 0.5 to 5 atm; quiescent; ISS CFI, 2017

conditions: 4 to 6 mm droplets; 21% O2 in N2; 0.5 and 0.75 atm; quiescent; ISS CFI, 2017
